papers.title: Synthetic process modeling for ring rolling via physics-guided GANs and analytical transfer learning
papers.abstract: Abstract Modeling metal forming processes, and specifically ring rolling as considered in this research, is crucial for process design and the development of new product variants. Although finite element simulations and analytical modeling are common practices to perform process predictions, they can still present limitations such as high computational time, adherence to reality, and modeling accuracy. Trying to address all the above, this research proposes a novel generative machine learning solution for the creation of accurate and physics-compliant synthetic data for the ring rolling process, enabling almost real time and accurate process modeling within latent space. The proposed data generation method is based on multivariate generative adversarial network (GAN) combined with a physics-guided neural network (PGNN) to incorporate constraints relevant to the ring rolling process and integrate them into an auxiliary loss granting physical consistency. The proposed GAN architecture is then annotated as a physics-guided auxiliary GAN (PG-A-GAN). The physical constraints introduced are relevant to an analytical slip-line model for the force, a surrogate model for the torque, volume consistency, and an analytical model for the time–diameter relationship. Considering the duality of the physical modeling approach for the force and torque, where data-driven machine learning is stirred by analytical models, the proposed approach is defined as analytical transfer learning. Findings reveal that employing PGNNs in the GANs learning process improves physical loss in data generation, combined with a slight increase in data distribution similarity with respect to experimental instances. To enable modeling of specific and customized rolling instances, a condition based on the final sought ring geometry was introduced, within an auxiliary classifier generative adversarial network (ACGAN) framework. The proposed architecture allows the generation of multivariate, physically constrained, rolling time series and highlights the feasibility of such a modeling approach within the latent space and might be extended to other manufacturing processes by adapting modeling and retraining the proposed architecture.

papers.title: ANN-based surrogate modeling of composite laminates for structural optimization of wave energy converters
papers.abstract: Wave energy converters (WECs) possess considerable renewable energy potential; however, their large-scale deployment remains constrained by structural durability limitations and high manufacturing costs in harsh marine environments. Composite materials offer favorable strength-to-weight characteristics, yet optimizing laminate configurations via conventional finite element analysis (FEA) is computationally intensive, limiting exploration of high-dimensional design spaces. This study proposes a surrogate-based structural optimization framework integrating high-fidelity FEA with machine learning for composite WEC buoy design. A parametric analysis of a truncated spheroidal buoy was performed in ANSYS, systematically varying material type, stacking sequence, ply orientation, and laminate thickness under wave loading to construct a structural response database. An artificial neural network, trained on this dataset (R² = 0.97, RMSE = 1.8 mm) and coupled with a genetic algorithm, identified Pareto-optimal laminate configurations minimizing deformation subject to mass constraints. Optimized designs, validated against independent FEA simulations, exhibited deviations below 5%, substantially reducing computational cost and enabling scalable composite WEC hull design.

papers.title: Coupling High-Throughput Density Functional Theory, Automated Experimentation, and Adaptive Experimental Design To Achieve Selective Rare-Earth Element Separations
papers.abstract: Developing new separation technologies for rare-earth elements is essential for sustaining the critical materials supply chain. Toward this end, we developed a pH-controlled solvent extraction strategy employing an aqueous-phase holdback agent to enable selective lanthanide separations, using an integrated computational, machine learning, and automated experimental high-throughput workflow. Database screening, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and initial experimental evaluation identified oxaloacetic acid as a promising holdback agent that enhanced selective extraction of four lanthanides (Nd, Eu, Dy, Ho) when paired with the di(2-ethylhexyl)phosphoric acid (HDEHP or D2EHPA) extractant. Within this framework, the dependence of lanthanide solvent extraction was determined across a multidimensional chemical matrix (pH, extractant concentration, holdback agent concentration, and salt concentration) using automated, high-throughput experiments coupled with multi-objective Bayesian Optimization. Through efficient exploration of a large experimental space, we discovered Eu, Dy, and Ho could be selectively extracted over Nd in acidic media at pH ∼2.0, while a modest decrease in pH to ∼0.5 shifted the selectivity to enable Eu separation from Dy and Ho. The use of multi-objective Bayesian Optimization quickly yielded a 4-fold increase in separation factors compared to our HDEHP-only system, eliminating the need for a complete grid-based, exhaustive sampling approach. Overall, this work establishes a hierarchical and data-driven framework to identify selective separation conditions and provides a foundation for accelerating separations discovery and design.

papers.title: Energy absorption analysis and multi-objective optimization of torsional honeycomb thin-walled structures
papers.abstract: Abstract Lightweight structures with high energy absorption (EA) capacity are important for modern engineering applications. Inspired by turtle shell and conch geometries, this study proposes a novel C-shaped re-entrant auxetic metamaterial twisted re-entrant auxetic honeycomb tube (CRM-TAHTS), which combines a C-shaped re-entrant auxetic cell with a helical configuration. PLA specimens with twist angles of 0°, 15°, 30°, and 45° were fabricated by fused deposition modeling, and their EA performance was evaluated through quasi-static compression tests and validated finite element simulations. The results show that the twisted configuration changes the deformation mode from horizontal layer-by-layer folding to inclined progressive folding with overall rotation, thereby delaying densification. At a twist angle of 15°, the specific energy absorption (SEA) reaches 15.23 J g −1 , which is 9.0% higher than that of the non-twisted counterpart. A full-factorial design with three factors—twist angle, length, and wall thickness—and 4 × 4 × 3 levels was then used to construct a quadratic response surface surrogate model. The model was coupled with a multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm to maximize SEA and minimize peak crushing force (PCF). The continuous optimum was identified as θ T = 16.211°, L = 30 mm, and b = 1.1789 mm, and was rounded to a manufacturable design of θ T = 15°, L = 30 mm, and b = 1.2 mm for validation. The validated manufacturable design differs from the continuous surrogate optimum by only 3.30% and 0.01% for SEA and PCF, respectively. These results indicate that CRM-TAHTS provides a promising lightweight energy-absorbing structure for bio-inspired thin-walled component design.
